reading.body:
CoreSpace is a boutique Dallas colocation provider founded in 2009 that operates one 30,000 square foot facility with 1 megawatt of conditioned power, running at under 30 percent utilization as of its June 2025 sale announcement.

The company serves over 200 customers with a six-person team and reported 2024 revenue of 1.3 million dollars. This scale places CoreSpace at the small end of the colocation market, focused on small and midsize business customers rather than hyperscale AI infrastructure. The facility's low utilization rate and modest power capacity indicate it was not positioned for or pursuing the high-density compute workloads now driving data center demand.

In June 2025, founder Liana Dunlap initiated a private asset sale through Hilco Streambank. The sale listing included IP addresses, trademarks, domain names, real estate, and hardware, with non-binding indications of interest due June 17, 2025. As of the research date, no completed transaction or new owner could be confirmed, so CoreSpace's current operating status and ownership remain uncertain.

This facility's sub-megawatt power capacity and utilization rate illustrate the constraint facing smaller colocation operators in an era of AI scaling. The transition from the 2009 founding model to exit in 2025 reflects the divergence between traditional colocation and the power-intensive, long-term commitment required for modern AI compute.
